title: Verify Mermaid readability across MarkShare surfaces
description:
## Outcome

The adaptive diagram experience is proven in the actual Editor Preview and published Share Link, not only in isolated component tests. Existing Mermaid safety and Markdown reading behaviour remain unchanged.

## Verification matrix

- Surfaces: desktop split Preview, mobile Preview tab, desktop Share Link, and mobile Share Link.
- Widths: 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420, and 320 pixels, including editor split changes at desktop widths.
- Themes: light and dark.
- Diagram shapes: a small diagram that fits, the representative eight-stage left-to-right flowchart, a much wider overflow case, a tall diagram, and samples from sequence, class, state, and ER syntax.
- Inputs: pointer, wheel, trackpad-style scrolling, keyboard-only use, and touch-size interaction.
- States: loading, successful render, invalid source fallback, source change, viewport resize, open viewer, close and reopen, and more than one diagram in a document.

## Work

- Add focused automated tests at the Mermaid component boundary for geometry, controls, state transitions, cleanup, and accessibility.
- Add integration coverage proving Preview and Share Link share the same component and adaptive policy.
- Retain hostile Mermaid tests for strict configuration, rejected interactive input, sanitization, and safe fallback.
- Perform and record browser checks for SVG readability, overflow cues, tooltip placement, focus order, gestures, overlay containment, and absence of page-level horizontal overflow.
- Confirm that non-diagram Markdown retains its existing text measures and rendering.
- Run the full repository verification suite.

## Out of scope

Do not weaken acceptance because jsdom lacks layout. Use controlled geometry fakes for deterministic component tests and real-browser checks for layout and gestures.
design:
## Authoritative verification contract

- Test product outcomes through the Mermaid presentation boundary and rendered surfaces. Avoid making CSS text matching the primary proof of adaptive behaviour.
- Stub ResizeObserver and SVG geometry explicitly in unit tests so fit, wide-lane, and overflow thresholds are deterministic.
- Use real Mermaid rendering in at least one browser verification path so sanitized SVG viewBox handling and internal IDs are exercised.
- Check keyboard focus containment and restoration with observable focus assertions. Check listener and body-state cleanup by closing and unmounting during active interactions.
- Treat Preview and Share Link parity as an invariant. A fix that exists on one surface only is incomplete.
- Preserve the existing Markdown safety test suite. Pan and zoom work must not broaden Mermaid input or output permissions.
- Record any gesture limitation that cannot be automated, with exact device or browser steps and observed result.
acceptance_criteria:
- The complete verification matrix has automated coverage or an explicit recorded browser result.
- The representative eight-stage flowchart no longer renders with approximately 5px labels; it uses the wider lane and readable horizontal overflow as designed.
- Fitting, wide, overflowing, tall, and multiple diagrams behave independently across Preview and Share Link.
- Expanded-view pointer, keyboard, wheel, trackpad, and touch behaviour is verified at supported viewport sizes.
- Light and dark themes, focus handling, tooltip access, reduced motion, resize, rerender, cleanup, and invalid fallback are verified.
- Non-diagram Markdown measure and existing strict Mermaid security outcomes do not regress.
- There is no page-level horizontal overflow at any supported width.
- npm test, npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm run build all pass.
notes: Verified 2026-08-14: automated 42-test suite plus browser checks at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420, and 320px; representative flow, dark tokens, mobile overlay, single SVG, focus restoration, and no page overflow.

title: Build the accessible expanded Mermaid viewer
description:
## Outcome

A reader can open a wide Mermaid diagram in a near-full-screen MarkShare overlay, see the complete diagram first, and inspect detail with predictable pan and zoom controls on desktop, keyboard, trackpad, and touch devices.

## Work

- Open the viewer only from the diagram expand icon.
- Use almost the full viewport with a small desktop margin and an edge-to-edge mobile layout.
- Show one diagram at a time. Do not add previous or next navigation.
- Start every opening in Fit mode and reset to Fit when the viewer closes, reopens, or receives new diagram output.
- Provide visible Zoom in, Zoom out, and Fit controls. Use 400% as the initial maximum zoom and keep the limit in one named policy value.
- Support pointer drag to pan, mouse-wheel zoom, two-finger trackpad pan, pinch zoom, plus and minus zoom shortcuts, arrow-key panning, and 0 for Fit.
- Close through the visible close control, Escape, or the backdrop. A pointer action within the viewer must not trigger backdrop close.
- Trap focus while open, give the overlay a useful accessible name, prevent background interaction, and restore focus to the originating expand icon after close.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences and clean up document listeners, pointer capture, body state, and gesture state on close and unmount.

## Out of scope

Do not use the browser Fullscreen API. Do not add export, copy, minimap, diagram editing, or gallery navigation.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Build a reusable accessible overlay primitive suitable for this diagram viewer rather than stretching the current fixed 520px publish dialog styles. Shared low-level backdrop and focus behaviour may be factored without changing publish behaviour.
- Keep viewport transform state behind one interface with Fit, zoomBy, zoomTo, and panBy operations. Buttons, keyboard, pointer, wheel, and touch all call the same operations.
- Derive Fit from the current SVG viewBox and live viewer bounds. Recompute it on viewer resize and mobile orientation change without exceeding 100% natural scale unless the reader explicitly zooms in.
- Constrain zoom from Fit or the smallest useful scale through the named 400% maximum. Keep enough of the diagram reachable that panning cannot permanently lose it outside the viewport.
- Do not mount the same Mermaid SVG string twice with duplicate internal IDs. Either move or portal one live diagram presentation, or render a second SVG with a unique Mermaid render ID and valid internal references.
- If a zoom library is selected, declare it as a direct dependency and wrap it behind the viewer transform interface. Do not import Mermaid transitive d3-zoom by accident.
- Prevent wheel handling outside the open viewer and preserve expected two-finger trackpad panning. Use non-passive listeners only where preventDefault is required.
- Accessibility behaviour is part of correctness, not a later visual QA task.
acceptance_criteria:
- Selecting the inline expand icon opens one labelled near-full-screen viewer and places focus inside it.
- The diagram initially fits the viewer and resets to Fit after close, reopen, source change, and responsive resize.
- Visible buttons, plus and minus, 0, arrow keys, mouse wheel, pointer drag, two-finger trackpad pan, and pinch gestures operate through one bounded transform model.
- Zoom cannot exceed the named 400% initial maximum and the diagram cannot become permanently unreachable through panning.
- Close, Escape, and backdrop close work; interaction inside the viewer does not close it; focus returns to the originating icon.
- Background content cannot receive focus or scroll while the viewer is open, and all global listeners and body state are removed after close or unmount.
- No duplicate SVG IDs or broken marker, clip-path, or style references occur while the viewer is open.
- Automated interaction and accessibility tests pass with type checking, lint, and production build.
notes: Implemented accessible 400% expanded viewer with shared transform controls, focus containment/restoration, and cleanup.

title: Present Mermaid diagrams with clear inline controls and overflow cues
description:
## Outcome

Every valid Mermaid diagram has a consistent token-based panel. Readers can identify wide content, move through it without losing readability, and discover the expanded viewer without cluttering diagrams that already fit.

## Work

- Give every successfully rendered Mermaid diagram a subtle panel with theme-token background, border, radius, and padding.
- Centre diagrams that fit. Start horizontally overflowing diagrams at the left edge.
- Preserve native horizontal wheel, trackpad, touch, keyboard, and scrollbar access to inline overflow.
- When content exists beyond the visible right edge, show a soft edge fade and the short text Scroll to view.
- Remove the text after the reader first scrolls that diagram. Keep edge fades synchronized with the actual left and right overflow boundaries.
- Show an icon-only expand control only when the adaptive sizing policy marks the diagram as needing the wide treatment.
- Place the control at the top-right in a dedicated area that never covers the SVG.
- Give the icon an accessible name and a concise tooltip on pointer hover and keyboard focus. Do not depend on hover for the accessible name or touch operation.
- Reset hint dismissal, overflow cues, and inline scroll position when changed Markdown creates a new diagram.

## Out of scope

This bead does not implement expanded-view pan and zoom, export actions, previous or next diagram navigation, or author configuration.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Consume the sizing result from markshare-9df.1. Do not create a second width or readability heuristic in the control frame.
- Keep panel, cue, and expand-control state local to each diagram instance so documents with several diagrams do not affect one another.
- Calculate fades from real scrollWidth, clientWidth, and scrollLeft state, including fractional values and resize changes. Treat the native scrollbar as functional input, not decoration.
- Use existing MarkShare tokens and focus-visible conventions in both themes. Do not introduce hard-coded light-only colours.
- Keep loading and invalid Mermaid fallback behaviour distinct. The successful diagram panel must not conceal the existing safe source fallback.
- The expand icon announces the expanded-view action to assistive technology even when its visible tooltip is absent on touch devices.
acceptance_criteria:
- All successfully rendered diagrams use the subtle panel in Preview and Share Link, in light and dark themes.
- Fitting diagrams are centred and do not show overflow guidance or an expand control.
- Adaptive wide diagrams begin at the left, remain horizontally scrollable, show accurate overflow fades, and initially show Scroll to view.
- The text hint disappears after the first horizontal interaction for that diagram while boundary fades remain accurate.
- The expand icon appears only for diagrams that need wide treatment, does not cover SVG content, has an accessible name, and exposes its tooltip on hover and focus.
- New Mermaid output resets the inline position and cue state.
- Component tests cover multiple independent diagrams, scrolling to both boundaries, resize, source change, keyboard focus, tooltip behaviour, and both themes; type checking, lint, and build pass.
notes: Implemented token panel, native overflow cues, per-diagram hint reset, and wide-only accessible expand control.

title: Establish adaptive Mermaid sizing and the wide document lane
description:
## Outcome

The shared Mermaid component can distinguish a diagram that fits the prose measure from one that would become unreadable, and the document layout gives only that diagram access to a wider lane.

## Work

- Normalize sanitized Mermaid SVG dimensions from a valid viewBox after every render.
- Observe the diagram lane when it mounts and whenever the Preview split, Reader viewport, mobile tab, font metrics, or window size changes.
- Preserve natural SVG size when it fits. Scale down only as far as 0.875 of natural size. Use the wide lane when the prose column would require a smaller scale.
- If the wider lane is still smaller than 0.875 of the natural SVG width, keep the SVG at the readable minimum and allow overflow.
- Keep ordinary Markdown content at 62ch in Preview and 66ch in Reader while allowing an adaptive diagram frame to use the available pane or page width with the existing page padding.
- Reset derived size and scroll state when Mermaid renders a new SVG for changed source.
- Handle missing, zero, malformed, or changing SVG geometry without throwing or bypassing the existing safe fallback.

## Out of scope

Do not add the visual scroll hint, expand button, expanded viewer, export actions, author sizing directives, or source rewriting in this bead.
design:
## Authoritative implementation contract

- Keep one Mermaid rendering path under MarkdownView. A focused Mermaid presentation component can be extracted from markdown.tsx, but Markdown interpretation remains the owner of recognition and safety policy.
- Base adaptation on sanitized SVG geometry, not source parsing or flowchart-only Mermaid configuration. The same algorithm must work for flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, and other SVG-backed Mermaid types.
- Model natural size, available prose width, available wide-lane width, effective scale, and overflow as explicit derived state. Avoid one-off CSS aspect-ratio heuristics.
- Prefer ResizeObserver at the diagram boundary and make observer setup, stale callbacks, and teardown deterministic in tests.
- Do not widen the entire article. The rendered document needs a stable readable-content lane plus an intentional diagram breakout mechanism.
- Preserve SVG aspect ratio and sharp vector rendering. Do not set a fixed diagram height or rasterize the output.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every rendered Mermaid SVG receives a valid natural-size and effective-scale decision from its viewBox.
- A diagram that fits remains in the readable content lane at natural size.
- A diagram that would fall below 0.875 scale uses the wider lane; if that lane is still insufficient, the SVG remains at 0.875 scale and overflows horizontally.
- Preview and Reader prose retain their 62ch and 66ch measures while adaptive diagrams use their available wider space.
- Resizing the editor split, viewport, or mobile layout recomputes the decision without stale state or leaked observers.
- Changed Mermaid source resets the sizing and scroll decision.
- Missing or malformed dimensions fail safely.
- Focused component tests cover fit, wide-lane, overflow, resize, rerender, and cleanup outcomes; type checking, lint, and build pass.
notes: Implemented adaptive viewBox sizing, 0.875 readable minimum, wide lane, resize/rerender cleanup tests.

title: Make Mermaid diagrams readable and explorable
description:
## Problem

Wide Mermaid diagrams are currently scaled to 100% of the narrow Markdown text measure. A representative eight-stage left-to-right flowchart has a 1804 by 62.5 SVG viewBox but renders at about 553 by 19 pixels in Preview. Its normal 16px labels become about 5px and cannot be read.

## Product outcome

Mermaid diagrams remain readable without making prose lines wider. Every diagram has a subtle container. A diagram that cannot fit the prose measure at a readable scale uses the wider document lane, preserves readable labels, and scrolls horizontally when needed. Wide diagrams can open in an accessible near-full-screen viewer with pan and zoom.

## Scope

- Apply one automatic policy to every Mermaid diagram type.
- Apply the same behaviour in Preview and the published Share Link on desktop and mobile.
- Keep prose at the existing 62ch Preview and 66ch Reader measures.
- Do not require author directives or silently rewrite diagram source.
- Do not add SVG or PNG export, diagram-gallery navigation, or browser Fullscreen API behaviour.
- Treat 400% as the initial maximum zoom and keep that policy easy to revise.

## Delivery slices

1. Establish adaptive Mermaid sizing and the wide document lane.
2. Add the common diagram container, overflow cues, and expand affordance.
3. Build the accessible expanded diagram viewer.
4. Verify the complete behaviour across routes, diagram types, themes, inputs, and responsive sizes.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the existing shared Markdown interpretation path. Preview and Reader must continue to render the same MarkdownView and one Mermaid security policy.
- Keep Mermaid initialization, strict input rejection, SVG sanitization, invalid-diagram fallback, sizing, and presentation behind one Mermaid diagram component boundary. Do not add a second renderer or duplicate policy in App.
- Determine presentation from the sanitized rendered SVG viewBox and the available container width. Do not parse Mermaid syntax, diagram direction, or diagram type to guess size.
- Preserve natural SVG size when it fits. A diagram may scale down only to an effective scale of 0.875, which maps Mermaid default 16px labels to about 14px. If the diagram still does not fit, widen its lane and then use horizontal overflow instead of further shrinking it.
- Keep Preview prose at 62ch and Reader prose at 66ch. Give only adaptive diagram frames access to the wider scroll container; do not widen headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code, or fallback source.
- Every successfully rendered diagram uses the same token-based panel. Diagrams that fit are centred. Overflowing diagrams start at the left edge.
- The expanded viewer must not mount duplicate copies of the same ID-bearing SVG. Reuse one live SVG presentation or render a separately identified SVG so marker, clip-path, and style references remain valid.
- If a pan or zoom package is used, add it as a direct dependency. Do not rely on Mermaid transitive dependencies.
- Treat focus management, keyboard interaction, pointer and touch input, reduced-motion preferences, theme parity, ResizeObserver behaviour, and cleanup as part of the component contract.
- Tests must observe component and user outcomes. CSS source-string checks alone do not prove this feature.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every Mermaid diagram has the agreed subtle container in Preview and Share Link.
- Diagrams stay at natural scale when possible and never shrink below the agreed effective 0.875 scale; wider content gets a wide lane and horizontal scrolling.
- Only diagrams that need the adaptive wide treatment expose an expand icon and overflow guidance.
- The expanded viewer provides the agreed accessible pan, zoom, Fit, close, reset, pointer, touch, and keyboard behaviour.
- Existing strict Mermaid input policy, SVG sanitization, invalid fallback, prose measures, and Preview/Reader equivalence remain intact.
- Automated tests, type checking, lint, production build, and documented responsive browser checks pass.
notes:
Coordination bead only. Implement through child beads markshare-9df.1 to markshare-9df.4 in dependency order; do not treat the epic itself as a coding slice.
All four delivery slices completed and verified.

title: Deepen the Document lifecycle before Edit Links
description:
## Why

The Editor and Reader currently construct InstantDB transactions, queries, rule parameters, timestamps, and failure meaning directly. The document test reproduces that third-party implementation with a Proxy. Edit Links, private images, expiry, and deletion would multiply this leakage.

## What to build

Deepen the Document lifecycle before adding Edit Links. Concentrate publication, reading, capability enforcement, timestamps, and lifecycle outcome translation in one module with a small interface. Put InstantDB behind the true external seam: an InstantDB adapter in production and an in-memory or mock adapter in tests.

Preserve the existing anonymous publish, Share Link, read-only Reader, and generic unavailable behaviour.

## Scope limits

Do not implement Edit Links, images, expiry, cleanup, or new product behaviour here. Do not introduce ports for dependencies that do not vary.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- The Document lifecycle module owns persistence orchestration and capability rules.
- UI modules must not import the raw InstantDB client or construct transaction/query DSL, ruleParams, IDs, or timestamps.
- InstantDB is the production adapter. Tests use a second adapter, making this a real seam.
- Translate third-party loading, missing, and failure states into domain outcomes inside the module.
- The module interface is the test surface. Tests assert publish/read/unavailable outcomes and do not recreate InstantDB internals.
- Replace obsolete helper-level or DSL-mock tests once equivalent interface tests exist; do not layer both suites.
- Keep route grammar and Markdown interpretation outside this module.
acceptance_criteria:
- Editor and Reader no longer construct InstantDB transactions, queries, rule parameters, IDs, or timestamps.
- One production InstantDB adapter and one in-memory or mock test adapter satisfy the Document lifecycle seam.
- Existing publish, Share Link, read-only Reader, and generic unavailable behaviour remain unchanged.
- Tests exercise lifecycle outcomes through the module interface without reproducing the InstantDB transaction/query DSL.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Add expiry and complete deletion
description:
## What to build

Documents never expire by default. An editor can set a local date/time expiry; access stops exactly at that time; manual deletion and the daily Vercel cleanup remove Document and image records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Share Link returns the same unavailable response for a deleted or expired Document immediately after its expiry time.
- [ ] Expired and deleted Documents, including their pasted images, are removed by the cleanup process within 24 hours.

## Blocked by

- Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing.
- Support private pasted images.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the deep Document lifecycle module from markshare-ntg with expiry evaluation, deletion, and cleanup outcomes.
- Reader callers receive the same unavailable outcome for missing, expired, and deleted Documents; storage details and reason distinctions must not leak across the interface.
- Manual deletion and scheduled cleanup share lifecycle rules so Document and image removal cannot drift.
- Keep the Vercel schedule/transport at an internal seam with production and test adapters only where behaviour genuinely varies.
- Test expiry at exact timestamps with an injected clock or equivalent deterministic mechanism; do not rely on wall-clock sleeps.
- Test complete Document-plus-image deletion through lifecycle outcomes rather than InstantDB internals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Documents never expire by default and become unavailable exactly at a configured expiry time.
- Missing, expired, and deleted Documents produce the same externally observable unavailable result.
- Manual deletion and scheduled cleanup remove the Document and all owned images within the agreed window.
- Expiry and cleanup tests are deterministic and exercise the Document lifecycle interface without wall-clock sleeps or raw InstantDB assertions.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Apply privacy, abuse, and public-information controls
description:
## What to build

MarkShare has no analytics or content logging; protects Share Links from search indexing and referrer leakage; gives private generic link previews; applies Vercel protection and rate limits; and publishes About, Privacy, and Acceptable Use pages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Share Links do not expose Document titles or content to search engines, link previews, referrers, analytics, or application logs.
- [ ] Public creation and image upload are rate-limited, and the public-information pages describe the agreed service behaviour.

## Blocked by

- Create and read a basic Markdown Document.
- Support private pasted images.
- Add expiry and complete deletion.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the navigation module established by markshare-yis for About, Privacy, and Acceptable Use destinations. Do not add route checks directly to App.
- The navigation module owns route recognition, precedence, URL construction, and unavailable outcomes. Unknown paths must not fall through to the Editor.
- Keep Share Link privacy behaviour local to the Document lifecycle and navigation modules: generic unavailable results, private metadata, no edit-capability leakage, and no content-derived public preview data.
- Analytics, logging, referrer, indexing, and rate-limit controls must be verified at their observable seams rather than inferred from configuration text alone.
- Public-information content may be static, but its route meaning belongs to the same navigation test surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Share Links expose no Document title or content to indexing, previews, referrers, analytics, or application logs.
- Creation and image upload are rate-limited and the public-information destinations describe the agreed behaviour.
- Public-information, Share Link, Edit Link, and unknown routes share one navigation test surface; unknown paths never open the Editor.
- Privacy and abuse controls are verified through observable outcomes and deployment configuration checks.
- Tests, type checking, lint, production build, and production-like verification pass.

title: Production-readiness and handover
description:
## What to build

Verify the finished MarkShare flows end to end, including accessibility and mobile behaviour; complete production deployment configuration; and document manual InstantDB export and recovery steps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The supported creation, editing, reading, image, expiry, deletion, privacy, and theme flows are verified in a production-like deployment.
- [ ] An owner can follow concise guidance to export data and understand the recovery limits of version one.

## Blocked by

- Make the editor resilient and responsive.
- Support private pasted images.
- Add expiry and complete deletion.
- Apply privacy, abuse, and public-information controls.
acceptance_criteria: MarkShare is ready to launch and hand over.

title: Support private pasted images
description:
## What to build

Authors can paste or drag PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF images into a Document. MarkShare stores them privately in InstantDB, inserts Markdown automatically, and serves them only through an available Share Link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pasting or dropping a supported image inserts it into the editor and renders it for readers.
- [ ] The 5 MB per-image and 20 images per-Document limits are enforced, and image access does not become public through a standalone file URL.

## Blocked by

- Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing.
- Deliver the complete Markdown reading experience.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Extend the deep Document lifecycle module from markshare-ntg for image ownership, limits, persistence, and capability-controlled retrieval.
- UI modules must not call InstantDB image storage directly or interpret Share/Edit capability rules.
- Feed safe Document-scoped image references into the shared Markdown interpretation module from markshare-txp; do not create a second rendering policy for images.
- A standalone file URL must never become an alternative seam that bypasses Document availability.
- Test image lifecycle outcomes through the Document lifecycle interface and rendered image safety through the Markdown interpretation interface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pasting or dropping PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF inserts a Document-scoped Markdown reference and renders through the shared interpretation module.
- The 5 MB per-image and 20-images-per-Document limits are enforced in the Document lifecycle module.
- Image retrieval follows Document capability and availability rules; standalone file access cannot bypass them.
- UI modules do not access InstantDB image persistence directly.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.

title: Make the editor resilient and responsive
description:
## What to build

The editor provides side-by-side Write and Preview on desktop, Edit and Preview tabs on mobile, browser-local recovery for unpublished work, and import of existing Markdown files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The authoring flow is usable on current desktop and mobile browsers.
- [ ] Unsaved local work recovers after an accidental close, but public content changes only after Save changes.

## Blocked by

- Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing.
- Deliver the complete Markdown reading experience.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Deepen the Editor session rather than extracting isolated event helpers.
- Keep draft state, published state, local recovery, Markdown import, save transitions, retry behaviour, pane state, split invariants, and cleanup rules together behind one module interface.
- DOM-specific pointer capture, CSS custom properties, body-class mutation, local storage, and breakpoint behaviour stay inside the implementation.
- Browser dependencies are local-substitutable with jsdom, local storage stand-ins, and synthetic pointer/keyboard events. Do not expose browser adapters through the external interface.
- Test complete session transitions and observable interaction outcomes: recover, import, edit, save, failure/retry, tab switch, split clamping, keyboard increments, reset, and drag cleanup.
- Replace CSS-string assertions when an observable behaviour test covers the same rule. Retain only exact stylesheet contracts that cannot be observed reliably in jsdom.
- Isolated drag, clamp, or word-count helper modules are shallow and do not satisfy this design.
acceptance_criteria:
- Desktop Write/Preview, mobile Edit/Preview tabs, local draft recovery, Markdown import, and explicit save work end to end.
- Unsaved work recovers after an accidental close while public Reader content changes only after save.
- Split dragging, clamping, keyboard movement, reset, pointer cancellation, and body-class cleanup have observable interaction tests.
- Editor session tests survive internal refactors and do not depend on CSS source-text matching where behaviour is observable.
- Tests, type checking, lint, production build, and documented responsive browser checks pass.

title: Deliver the complete Markdown reading experience
description:
## What to build

Readers get safe GitHub-style Markdown, highlighted code, tables, task lists, footnotes, strict Mermaid rendering, title extraction from the first heading, and a Download .md button.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Supported Markdown constructs render reliably without allowing raw HTML or unsafe Mermaid behaviour.
- [ ] The Document title follows the first top-level heading rule and readers can download the Markdown source.

## Blocked by

- Create and read a basic Markdown Document.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- Build one deep Markdown interpretation module shared by Preview, Reader, title derivation, metadata, and source download.
- The claim that Preview matches the Share Link is an invariant: both must use the same interpretation policy and must not duplicate renderer configuration.
- Keep this module in-process. Do not add an adapter for pure parsing or rendering.
- Safe GitHub-style Markdown, raw-HTML rejection, highlighting, tables, task lists, footnotes, and strict Mermaid behaviour live behind the module interface.
- The module interface is the test surface. Cover supported syntax and hostile inputs through it, then replace overlapping title-helper and incidental whole-App tests.
- A thin React render pass-through is shallow and does not satisfy this design.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preview and Reader use one shared Markdown interpretation module and produce equivalent document output.
- Supported GitHub-style syntax, highlighting, tables, task lists, footnotes, and strict Mermaid rendering work without raw HTML or unsafe Mermaid behaviour.
- The first top-level heading determines the Document title and the Markdown source downloads correctly.
- Renderer configuration and safety policy are not duplicated across UI call sites.
- Tests exercise supported and hostile inputs through the module interface; tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #3. Preview and Reader share one Markdown interpretation module with GFM syntax, highlighting, strict and sanitized Mermaid, first-heading titles, and exact-source downloads. Verified: 27 tests, typecheck, lint, and production build pass; independent standards and spec reviews have no remaining material findings.

title: Bootstrap the MarkShare application
description:
## What to build

A deployable MarkShare shell on Vercel with InstantDB configuration, the agreed calm visual
foundation, Light/Dark/System theme selection, and a responsive home page that starts document
creation.

The visual foundation is no longer open to interpretation. It was settled by a three-variant UI
prototype (Split Desk / Paper / Console); **Split Desk won**. The full, authoritative interface
specification — colour tokens, typography, layout metrics, component specs, responsive rules and
interaction behaviour — is in the Design section of this issue, and the working reference
implementation is `prototype/ui/markshare-ui-prototype.html` with notes in
`prototype/ui/README.md`.

Build the design system and the app shell here. Later issues fill the shell in:
`markshare-xpb` (create and read), `markshare-txp` (rendering pipeline), `markshare-yis`
(edit links and explicit publishing), `markshare-2ck` (editor responsiveness and drafts).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The application runs locally and can deploy to Vercel with its required configuration
      documented.
- [ ] The home page provides a clear Create a document path and persists the selected System,
      Light, or Dark theme.
- [ ] The design tokens in the Design section exist as the single source of truth for colour,
      typography, spacing and radii, and both themes are driven by one `data-theme` switch.
- [ ] The shell fills the viewport at every window size with no page-level scroll and no
      horizontal overflow: verified at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420 and 320 wide.
- [ ] The two documented breakpoints behave as specified — 900px (panes to tabs) and 620px
      (condensed top bar).

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
design:
# MarkShare interface specification — authoritative

Settled by prototype round 1 (Split Desk vs Paper vs Console). Split Desk won. Reference
implementation: `prototype/ui/markshare-ui-prototype.html`. Screenshots: `prototype/ui/shots/`.

The prototype is throwaway code — copy the *design*, not the implementation. Anything below marked
PROTOTYPE ONLY must not be carried across.

## 1. Design tokens

Both themes are driven by one attribute on `<html>`: `data-theme="light" | "dark"`. The stored
preference is `system | light | dark`; `system` resolves against
`matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` and must re-resolve live when the OS setting changes.

Light:

    --paper      #faf9f6   app background, write surface
    --surface    #ffffff   bars, preview, cards
    --surface-2  #f3f1ec   hover fills, segmented control track
    --sunken     #efece5   code blocks, link boxes, inline code
    --ink        #232019   primary text
    --ink-soft   #5d574c   secondary text, code text
    --ink-faint  #8f887a   labels, metadata, footer
    --line       #e6e1d6   structural borders
    --line-soft  #f0ece3   internal dividers, table rules
    --accent     #3f6f5c   primary buttons, active divider, checked boxes
    --accent-soft #e4efe9  accent chips
    --accent-ink #2c5344   accent text on soft accent
    --warn       #8a5a2b   unsaved state
    --danger     #8f3a3a   delete

Dark:

    --paper      #15161a
    --surface    #1b1d22
    --surface-2  #22252b
    --sunken     #101114
    --ink        #e9e7e0
    --ink-soft   #a9a49a
    --ink-faint  #7b756b
    --line       #2c3038
    --line-soft  #23262c
    --accent     #7fb79c
    --accent-soft #1f3129
    --accent-ink #a9d4c1
    --warn       #c69a63
    --danger     #d98a8a

Shared: `--radius: 10px`;
`--shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(35,32,25,.05), 0 8px 24px rgba(35,32,25,.06)` (dark:
`0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.3), 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.35)`).

Primary button text is `#fff` in light and `#10231c` in dark — do not use `--paper`.

## 2. Typography

- Interface and rendered document: **Inter**, weights 400/500/600/700, with
  `font-feature-settings: "cv05" 1, "ss03" 1` (single-storey l, curved r). Self-host it; do not
  ship a Google Fonts request to production. Fallback: `ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, "Segoe UI",
  system-ui, sans-serif`.
- Markdown source, link URLs and metadata: `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`.
  Column alignment matters in tables and code, so the Write pane is never proportional.
- Base: 15px / 1.5.
- Rendered document: h1 1.9em/1.2 weight 650 tracking -0.022em; h2 1.32em weight 640 tracking
  -0.014em with 1.9em top margin; h3 1.08em weight 650; h4 1em weight 650 in `--ink-soft`.
  Paragraph bottom margin 1.05em.
- Measure: preview column `max-width: 62ch` centred; reader column `max-width: 66ch` at 16px.

## 3. Shell layout — author surface

Single full-height column, top to bottom:

1. **App bar**, 56px, `--surface`, 1px `--line` bottom border. Left: 20px rounded mark
   (`--accent`, radius 6px) + "MarkShare" at weight 700, tracking -0.015em. Then a 1px `--line`
   separator and the document title (weight 560, truncates with ellipsis) followed by the save-state
   chip. Right, in order: theme toggle (quiet), Share (secondary), Save changes (primary).
2. **Tab strip**, only below 900px — a segmented control (Edit / Preview) on a `--sunken` track,
   3px padding, 9px radius; the active segment is `--surface` with `--shadow`.
3. **Pane row**, fills remaining height. CSS grid:
   `grid-template-columns: var(--split, 50%) 7px 1fr`.
   - Write pane: 40px head ("WRITE" label + formatting tools, right-aligned), then a full-height
     textarea, `--paper`, mono 13.4px / 1.75, padding 22px 24px.
   - Divider: the 7px middle column. See §5.
   - Preview pane: 40px head ("PREVIEW" label + a mono note reading "matches share link" or
     "not yet published"), then the scrolling rendered document on `--surface`, padding 32px 40px.
4. **Status footer**, 32px, 11.5px `--ink-faint`: word count, `n/20` images, expiry state, and the
   share URL pushed right in mono.

Labels ("WRITE", "PREVIEW", field labels) are 11px, weight 700, uppercase, 0.06em tracking,
`--ink-faint`.

## 4. Shell layout — reader surface

What a share-link recipient sees. 52px bar: mark, document title, a "Read only" chip, then expiry
text, Download .md, theme toggle. Below it the rendered document scrolls **inside its own
container** (not the page), padding 56px 24px 120px, 66ch measure at 16px.

No editing affordances may appear on this surface. Nothing here may leak the edit link.

## 5. The resizable divider

- Grid column of 7px. The visible line is a 1px `--line` rule centred in it, plus a resting grip:
  3px × 28px, radius 3px, `--ink-faint` at 0.5 opacity, so it reads as draggable before hover.
- Hover / focus / drag: the rule thickens to 3px and turns `--accent`; the resting grip fades out.
- Cursor `col-resize`; `touch-action: none` so pointer drags work on touch devices.
- **Drag** sets the split as a percentage of the pane row's width, clamped to **22%–78%**.
- **Double-click** resets to **50%**.
- **Keyboard**: it is a real `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`,
  `aria-valuenow/min/max`, in the tab order. `←`/`→` nudge 2%, with Shift 10%; `Home` resets.
  `aria-valuenow` updates as it moves.
- Dragging must not re-render the document: write the percentage to a CSS custom property on the
  pane row and update state without a redraw. Add a body-level `user-select: none; cursor:
  col-resize` for the duration of the drag and remove it on pointerup.
- The split position survives re-renders. Below 900px the divider is `display: none`.

## 6. Responsive rules

The shell owns the window. `html, body { height: 100%; overflow: hidden }`, the app root is
`height: 100%`, and the shell is `min-height/max-height: 100dvh`. Every scroll happens inside a
pane. The page itself must never scroll — that is what pushed the app bar off-screen in an earlier
build.

- **≥ 900px** — two panes, divider live.
- **< 900px** — divider hidden, grid collapses to one column, Edit / Preview tabs shown, only the
  selected pane rendered. Preview padding drops to 24px 20px.
- **< 620px** — Share collapses to an icon (↗), "Save changes" becomes "Save", the wordmark is
  hidden so the document title keeps its space, and the "Saved" chip is dropped. **The amber
  unsaved dot must always survive** — explicit publishing depends on it being visible. The footer
  hides the share URL; the reader bar hides the expiry text.

Verify at 1920, 1440, 1280, 1024, 900, 768, 620, 420 and 320 wide: shell fills the viewport, no
page scroll, no horizontal overflow.

## 7. Components

- **Button**: radius 8px, padding 7px 13px, 13.5px weight 500, 1px `--line` border on `--surface`;
  hover fills `--surface-2`. Small: 5px 9px / 12.5px. Primary: `--accent` fill and border. Quiet:
  transparent border and fill, `--ink-soft` text.
- **Chip / pill**: radius 999px, padding 3px 9px, 11.5px weight 600. Saved = `--surface-2` on
  `--line-soft`. Unsaved = transparent fill, `--warn` text and border, with a 6px `--warn` dot.
- **Link box** (share / edit link): `--sunken` fill, 1px `--line-soft`, radius 8px, padding
  9px 11px; mono URL truncating with ellipsis, Copy button on the right.
- **Publish modal**: scrim `rgba(20,18,14,.42)`; card `min(520px, 100%)`, radius 14px, padding
  24px, `--shadow`. Contents in order: heading "Your document is live", the line "Anyone with the
  share link can read it. No one can change it.", the read-only share link, the private edit link
  labelled "keep it safe", expiry set/remove, then Delete document (danger, quiet) and Done.
  Clicking the scrim closes; clicking the card does not; `Esc` closes.
- **Toast**: centred pill above the bottom edge, `--ink` fill with `--paper` text, ~1.9s. It must
  not own rendering — an action fired while an earlier toast is up still has to redraw.

## 8. Behaviour the shell must get right

- **Explicit publishing.** The draft is allowed to run ahead of the published document. The
  save-state chip flips to "Unsaved changes" **as the author types**, not on blur or on save, and
  the preview head switches to "not yet published". `⌘S` / `Ctrl+S` saves.
- **Title rule.** The document title is the first `# ` heading, else "Untitled document":
  `md.split("\n").find(l => l.startsWith("# "))?.slice(2).trim()`.
- **Theme.** Toggle cycles system → light → dark. Persist the choice; resolve `system` live.
- **Reader shows the saved version**, never the draft.
- Typing must not lose caret position or scroll position, and must not re-render the textarea.

## 9. Not covered by the prototype

- **The home page / creation entry point** in this issue's scope was never prototyped. Build it
  from these tokens: same 56px bar, one clear "Create a document" primary action, theme control
  present. Anything beyond that is a fresh design decision — do not invent a dashboard.
- The Markdown pipeline itself belongs to `markshare-txp`: sanitised GitHub-flavoured Markdown,
  no raw HTML, strict Mermaid. The prototype's renderer is a toy for layout only.

## 10. PROTOTYPE ONLY — do not port

Fake in-memory document and links; fake copy-to-clipboard; the decorative B / I / H / link / code /
image toolbar (no behaviour behind it); the floating "PROTOTYPE" bar and its Author/Reader toggle;
`innerHTML` re-rendering; the toy Markdown renderer; the Google Fonts `<link>`.

## 11. Known open questions

- Preview scroll does not follow the cursor; with a wide Write pane the two sides drift. Decide
  whether scroll sync is in scope for version one.
- The formatting toolbar needs real behaviour, or should be dropped from the first build.
- Whether the split position should persist per browser (localStorage) or reset each session.
acceptance_criteria: The deployable themed application shell and creation entry point work end to end, built on the design tokens and responsive rules recorded in the Design section, with no page-level scroll or horizontal overflow at any window size.
close_reason: Implemented by commits 9ac408e and 295734a; responsive shell, theme persistence, documented setup, and Split Desk design are present. Verified 2026-08-13: 19 tests, type checking, and lint pass.

title: Create and read a basic Markdown Document
description:
## What to build

Anyone can write Markdown in the browser, publish it without an account, receive a hard-to-guess Share Link, and open that link to read the rendered Document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publishing creates a persistent Document and a unique read-only Share Link.
- [ ] A visitor with the Share Link can read the rendered Document, while an unknown or unavailable link does not disclose content.

## Blocked by

- Bootstrap the MarkShare application.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous creation and read-only sharing work end to end.
close_reason: Implemented by commit 928e024 with follow-up fixes b487532 and 35b3a17; anonymous publication, opaque Share Link reading, read-only Reader, and generic unavailable behaviour are covered by passing tests.

title: Add separate Edit Links and manual publishing
description:
## What to build

Authors receive a private Edit Link; the same browser remembers edit access; Share Link recipients remain read-only; edits publish only when the author saves; authors can delete a Document or replace a leaked Edit Link.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Share Link cannot modify a Document; an Edit Link can modify, revoke, or replace it.
- [ ] The author must save changes explicitly before readers see them, and returning in the same browser restores edit access.

## Blocked by

- Create and read a basic Markdown Document.
design:
## Authoritative architecture

- This work depends on markshare-ntg. Extend the deep Document lifecycle module; do not reintroduce raw InstantDB transactions, queries, rule parameters, timestamps, or capability rules in UI modules.
- The lifecycle module owns Share Link versus Edit Link capability meaning, explicit publication, revocation, rotation, deletion requests, and domain outcomes.
- Establish saved-versus-draft transitions in the Editor session so the Reader always sees the saved version. Keep transition rules together rather than scattering them across event handlers.
- Once the exact Edit Link path grammar is chosen, deepen Share/Edit Link routing: one navigation module owns recognition, capability interpretation, URL construction, and browser-history behaviour. Unknown non-root routes must resolve as unavailable, not as the Editor.
- Browser history is local-substitutable; keep browser details internal rather than exposing a new port.
- Test lifecycle, capability, saved-versus-draft, route round trips, malformed paths, and unknown paths through stable interfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
- Share Links remain read-only; Edit Links can edit, save, revoke or rotate access, and request deletion.
- The same browser restores edit access without disclosing the Edit Link to Share Link readers.
- Draft changes remain private until explicit save, and Reader output always reflects the saved version.
- UI modules do not construct InstantDB operations or capability rule parameters.
- Share/Edit route recognition and construction have one test surface; malformed and unknown routes disclose nothing and never open the Editor.
- Tests, type checking, lint, and production build pass.
